column1: # Gate: scripts/ci/pip-audit-gate.sh, run by the `supply-chain:pip-audit` job.
# MEASURED 2026-08-04 with pip-audit 2.10.1 against PyPI + the PyPI advisory
# database. 34 unique (package, advisory) pairs across FOUR packages. Every row
# below was produced by the tool; none was guessed.
# READ THIS BEFORE TREATING THE LIST AS ROUTINE DEBT. IT IS NOT.
# All four packages sit in the request path of `/v1/scan-file`, the endpoint
# that accepts an uploaded document from a customer and parses it:
#     python-multipart  parses the multipart upload itself
#     starlette         reconstructs the URL and handles the request
#     pillow            decodes image pages and writes redacted output
# These are not transitive libraries that happen to be installed — they are the
# code that touches untrusted bytes first. Several of the advisories are
# denial-of-service or path-traversal reachable from exactly that input
# (CVE-2026-24486 path traversal in python-multipart; CVE-2026-42310 a PDF that
# hangs Pillow indefinitely; CVE-2025-70559 privilege escalation in
# WHY THEY ARE BASELINED RATHER THAN FIXED IN THE SAME COMMIT: the fixes are
# real dependency upgrades, not patch bumps —
#     Pillow            <12     -> >=12.3   the pin's own upper bound must move,
# and this workstream is CI configuration. Landing an untested upgrade of the
# document-parsing stack alongside a pipeline change would be the more
# dangerous of the two options. The gate exists so the number cannot grow
# quietly while that work is scheduled.
# FOLLOW-UP WS6-2-FU1: take the two direct pins (python-multipart, pdfminer.six)
# first — 9 of 34, no API surface shared with our code beyond the parse call —
# then Pillow, then fastapi/starlette last. Each needs `test:ml-sidecar` green.
# The key is (package, advisory-id) — deliberately NOT the version. Three of
# the four constraints in requirements.txt are ranges (`cryptography>=42`,
# drifts with time and no repository change. Keying on the version would turn
# every upstream patch release into a wall of spurious "new" and "stale" rows.
# The `resolved=` column is INFORMATIONAL — the version seen on 2026-08-04 —
# The gate fails in BOTH directions, like scripts/ci/fmt-gate.sh:
#   * an advisory NOT in this file      -> FAIL, something new appeared.
#   * a row here no longer reported     -> FAIL, delete it; the list must shrink.
# So the debt can only go down, and it cannot rot into a permanent excuse list.
# Columns: package <TAB> advisory <TAB> cve <TAB> resolved-version <TAB> fix
